# Metrics reference

<!-- Generated by sidecar/cmd/gen_metrics_doc from sidecar/internal/metricsreg;
do not edit. Regenerate with: cd sidecar && go generate ./internal/metricsreg/ -->

pg_sage serves the Prometheus text format on `/metrics`: on the separate
listener (`prometheus.listen_addr`) and, with `prometheus.serve_on_api`,
on the API port behind a token; [Deployment](deployment.md) shows the scrape
configuration.

Every family pg_sage exports is listed here. **Modes** names the operating
modes that render the family ("all" is standalone, fleet and meta). **Since**
is the first release that exported it under this name. A family whose data
does not exist yet (no TLS, no SLOs, no failure so far) has no samples.

Alert rules ship in [`deploy/prometheus/pg_sage.rules.yml`](https://github.com/jasonmassie01/pg_sage/blob/master/deploy/prometheus/pg_sage.rules.yml),
tested by [`pg_sage.rules_test.yml`](https://github.com/jasonmassie01/pg_sage/blob/master/deploy/prometheus/pg_sage.rules_test.yml)
with `promtool test rules`; each alert links its runbook below.

## Process and scrape

The build, the mode, the control database connection, leases and how fresh each database's metrics refresh is.

| Metric | Type | Labels | Unit | Modes | Since | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pg_sage_build_info` | gauge | `version`, `commit` | - | all | v2.6.0 | pg_sage build: version and commit |
| `pg_sage_connection_up` | gauge | - | - | all | v0.7.0 | 1 if the sidecar reaches its control database (YAML fleet: any database); per database see pg_sage_database_up |
| `pg_sage_info` | gauge | `version`, `mode` | - | all | v0.1.0 | pg_sage version |
| `pg_sage_leader` | gauge | `scope` | - | all | v2.6.0 | Whether this sidecar holds the scope's lease and may run leader-only jobs (1) or follows (0) |
| `pg_sage_leader_last_renew_age_seconds` | gauge | `scope` | seconds | all | v2.6.0 | Seconds since the last successful lease store round trip (since start when none yet) |
| `pg_sage_leader_transitions_total` | counter | `scope` | - | all | v2.6.0 | Leader/follower changes of this sidecar, lapses included |
| `pg_sage_metrics_listener_up` | gauge | - | - | all | v2.6.0 | 1 when the separate /metrics listener (prometheus.listen_addr) is serving, 0 when it failed to bind |
| `pg_sage_metrics_refresh_success` | gauge | `database`, `source` | - | all | v2.6.0 | 1 if the database's last metrics refresh of the source succeeded |
| `pg_sage_metrics_refresh_timestamp_seconds` | gauge | `database`, `source` | seconds | all | v2.6.0 | Unix time of the source's last successful metrics refresh |
| `pg_sage_mode` | gauge | - | - | all | v0.7.0 | Operating mode (0=meta, 1=standalone, 2=fleet) |
| `process_start_time_seconds` | gauge | - | seconds | all | v2.6.0 | Start time of the process since the Unix epoch in seconds |

| `pg_sage_fleet_instance_health` | `pg_sage_database_health_score` | - | v2.6.0 |
| `pg_sage_connections_total` | - | use postgres_exporter's pg_stat_activity_count | v2.6.0 |
| `pg_sage_cache_hit_ratio` | - | use postgres_exporter's pg_stat_database_blks_hit and pg_stat_database_blks_read | v2.6.0 |
| `pg_sage_optimizer_recommendations_total` | `pg_sage_optimizer_recommendations` | renamed: a gauge, not a counter | v2.6.0 |
| `pg_sage_fleet_findings_total` | `pg_sage_fleet_findings_open` | renamed: a gauge, not a counter | v2.6.0 |

<!-- metrics-renames:end -->

## Alert runbooks

### PgSageDown

**Severity:** page. **Fires when:** Prometheus has not scraped a pg_sage target (`up == 0`) for 5 minutes.

**What to do:** Check that the sidecar process or pod runs and that the scrape reaches `/metrics` (the listener's `pg_sage_metrics_listener_up` is 0 when it could not bind). The rule matches `job="pg_sage"`; edit it if your scrape job has another name.

### PgSageDatabaseDown

**Severity:** page. **Fires when:** `pg_sage_database_up` has been 0 for 5 minutes: the database is unreachable or its status refresh fails.

**What to do:** Open the database's page in the dashboard for the last error, check the database and the network path, and the sidecar log for `[fleet]` warnings. Nothing is collected or acted on while it is down.

### PgSageCollectorStale

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** The collector's last snapshot is older than 3 intervals (180 s at the default `collector.interval_seconds` of 60).

**What to do:** Check `pg_sage_collector_breaker_state` (1 skipping, 2 dormant under load) and `pg_sage_collector_persist_failures_total`. Raise the 180 in the rule if you set a longer collector interval.

### PgSageLLMCircuitOpen

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** The LLM circuit breaker has been open for 15 minutes; model-backed features fall back to rules.

**What to do:** Check the provider's status, the API key and `pg_sage_llm_tokens_used_today` against `pg_sage_llm_tokens_budget_daily`; see the LLM setup guide.

### PgSageActionFailed

**Severity:** page. **Fires when:** An action failed in the last 15 minutes: its outcome counter rose, or the database's first failure was recorded.

**What to do:** Read the action log in the dashboard (Actions) for the error and what was rolled back. pg_sage tries the change again on later cycles until it has failed three times for that object, so fix the cause or hold it with the emergency stop.

### PgSageActionRolledBack

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** An action was rolled back in the last hour, by verification (a regression) or by hand. A Prometheus with no history of the last hour also reports earlier rollbacks once.

**What to do:** Read the verification verdict in the action log. A rolled-back finding is not applied again for `trust.rollback_cooldown_days` (7 by default).

### PgSageSelfBudgetExceeded

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** pg_sage has used more than its declared budget of a resource for 15 minutes (`self_budget`).

**What to do:** Compare `pg_sage_self_*` with `pg_sage_self_budget`; lengthen collector or analyzer intervals, or raise the budget if the load is expected.

### PgSageSLOPage

**Severity:** page. **Fires when:** An SLO's error budget is burning at page rate (`pg_sage_slo_state{state="page"}`).

**What to do:** Open the SLO in the dashboard for the burning window and the incidents Sage SRE linked to it.

### PgSageInvestigationBacklogOld

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** A Sage SRE investigation has been open for over an hour.

**What to do:** Check `pg_sage_sre_investigations` by state: runs in `needs_evidence` wait for a probe or a person, and `pg_sage_sre_probe_refusals_total` shows probe slots running out.

### PgSageTLSCertExpiring

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** The certificate the API serves expires within 14 days (`pg_sage_api_tls_cert_not_after_seconds`), for an hour. Only a sidecar serving the API over TLS exports it; `/ready` reports `tls_expiring` from the same 14 days.

**What to do:** Renew the certificate and replace the files `SAGE_TLS_CERT` and `SAGE_TLS_KEY` name; the next new TLS connection to the API loads the pair (files checked at most every 5 s), without a restart. A kept-alive scrape connection does not, so on an idle API open the dashboard once and the gauge follows. If the alert stays, check `pg_sage_api_tls_reload_failures_total` and the log for the reload error: a failed reload keeps the old certificate.

### PgSageLeaderLeaseStale

**Severity:** page. **Fires when:** A sidecar has not reached its lease store for a scope in over 90 s (three lease TTLs), for 2 minutes (`pg_sage_leader_last_renew_age_seconds`).

**What to do:** A leader that cannot renew loses the lease and stops its jobs; a follower that cannot read it cannot take over. Check the sidecar's connection to the database that holds `sage.fleet_leader_lease` and the log for `leader:` warnings, then `pg_sage_leader` to see which replica leads now.

### PgSageSSODiscoveryDown

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** OAuth is enabled but OIDC discovery has not succeeded for 15 minutes (`pg_sage_sso_discovery_ready` 0), so SSO sign-in cannot start.

**What to do:** Check that the sidecar reaches the issuer's `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and that `oauth.issuer_url` is right; `pg_sage_sso_discovery_failures_total` counts the failed attempts.

### PgSageApprovalsWaiting

**Severity:** ticket. **Fires when:** A database has had actions of one risk waiting for approval for a day (`pg_sage_actions_pending_approval` above 0 throughout).

**What to do:** Open the approval queue in the dashboard (Actions) and approve or reject them. Pending approvals do not run on their own; a queue nobody reads means the changes Sage proposed are not being made.
